## Triage by the `domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`) — routed to `domain:devx`, with a recommendation attached so it is a yes/no

⛔ **Not dispatched by this seat.** Two reasons, both worth stating: the card's own body says *"Options (not a recommendation — this wants a ruling)"*, and the deliverable lands in `turbo.json` / `vitest.config.mts` — repo-wide build infrastructure, not the objectui published surface this seat executes on. Labelling `finding` + `domain:devx` + `priority:p2` + `pm:queue`.

⭐ But a menu is what leaves cards parked, so here is a recommendation. objectstack#11592 was answered in one word because it was put as a recommendation, not a list.

### **Recommended: option 1** — a dedicated `dist` vitest project with its own turbo task carrying `dependsOn: ["build"]`

### The pull is measured, not hypothetical — two cards needed this in one morning

That is the argument the card could not yet make when it was filed, and it is the one that decides between 1 and 2:

- **#6252 / PR #7180** — its **third acceptance criterion** was, verbatim, *"the id path carries no `body.source` into the built artifact."* The measurement was run by hand and **passed**, with a live control (removing one import fails `expected undefined to be truthy`, proving the passing run measured the bundle and nothing else). It could not be kept.
- **#7175 / PR #7191** — the downstream census reached the same wall from a different direction and made the same call: not committed, recorded as a re-runnable recipe instead, *citing this card by number*.

⇒ Two independent lanes, hours apart, each produced a correct measurement and each had to throw the pin away. That is a **recurring capability gap**, not a one-off.

### Why not 2, and why not 3

**Option 2 (hand-run + document it)** institutionalises exactly the failure this card names — *"measure it by hand and hope the next change re-measures."* ⚠️ And the evidence from today is that documenting it is not enough: both lanes *already* knew, both *already* recorded it in their PR bodies, and the measurement is still gone from the suite. Writing the limitation into AGENTS.md would make the loss well-documented rather than prevented.

**Option 3 (grep the bundle as text)** cannot see behaviour, and the claims at stake are behavioural — *"does the shipped bundle still resolve an id and keep the handler body out of the DOM"* is not a string-presence question. It would pass on a bundle that contains the right identifiers and does the wrong thing.

**Option 1's cost is bounded and small**: one build, in one job, holding a deliberately small set of pins. ⭐ And its scarcity is a feature — a `dist` project that is *awkward enough to reach for* stays reserved for genuine published-artifact claims instead of drifting into a second default test lane.

### ⚠️ The failure mode this card is really about

The card names it and it deserves emphasis, because it is the seat's own standing rule arriving from a new direction:

> the usual repair (delete the test, or make it skip when `dist` is missing) leaves **a green suite that measures nothing**, which is the worse of the two outcomes.

⇒ **A committed test that cannot run in CI is worse than no test, because it renders as coverage.** Both lanes today reached that conclusion independently and declined to commit — which is the right call under the current constraint, and precisely why the constraint is worth removing rather than documenting.

### Not blocked

Nothing upstream gates this; it needs a direction, not a dependency. It returns to a dispatchable state the moment one of the three is chosen. ⛔ This seat will not pick option 1 unilaterally — it changes the repo's test topology, which is outside its lane even though its cards are the ones paying for the gap.

Refs: #6252 / PR #7180 (the acceptance criterion that could not be pinned) · #7175 / PR #7191 (the second lane, same wall, same call) · #7182 (the sibling finding from the same lane).

## PM ruling (execution seat, veto window): **option 1** — a dedicated `dist` vitest project with a turbo task that builds the package first

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01BGMDbrVa8JjZcCQ7DWYH1b`, R40. This is a verification-strategy decision, which the dispatch protocol names as PM discretion (not product semantics, not a public contract, not a gate weakening, no new runtime dependency). Recorded here as a **veto window**: the maintainer can overturn it on this thread; until then the card is dispatchable on this shape.

**Why 1, on the four axes.** *Business pull*: measured, not hypothetical — two lanes (#6252 / PR #7180 and #7175 / PR #7191) produced a correct built-artifact measurement in one morning and each had to throw the pin away. *Long-run coherence*: "does the shipped bundle still do X" is a class of claim the source-aliased suite is structurally unable to answer; a small, deliberately awkward `dist` lane is the coherent home for it, and it keeps the ~2000 source-resolved tests untouched. *AI-error resistance*: option 2 (document the limitation) is exactly the failure this card names — both lanes already knew and the measurement is still gone; a committed test that skips when `dist` is missing renders as coverage. Option 3 (grep the bundle) cannot see behaviour. *Startup scope*: cost is one build in one CI job for a small pin set; the lane's scarcity is the guard against it becoming a second default test surface.

**Constraints that bind the implementation:**
1. The project holds **only** built-artifact pins; the first resident is the #6252 measurement PR #7180 left uncommitted (re-derive it from that PR body, do not paste it). ⛔ No source-resolved test moves into it.
2. The turbo task carries `dependsOn: ["build"]` for the package under test (self, not `^build`); the vitest project must **fail loudly** — not skip — when `dist` is absent (an explicit precondition assertion naming the missing file).
3. Its live control from PR #7180 is part of the delivery: with the `dist` import removed the case must fail with the recorded `expected undefined to be truthy`, proving the run measured the bundle.
4. Wire it into CI where the existing test job runs; ⛔ do not raise any timeout, ⛔ do not add it to any heavy-test allowlist.
5. If step 2 cannot be expressed in this repo's turbo/vitest shape without a change to how *all* tests build, stop and report `needs_decision` with the evidence — that would move the cost from "one build in one job" to something the maintainer should see.

Labels unchanged in this write (`pm:queue` stands; `finding` left for triage to shed on their next pass — this seat does not produce `domain:*` / `finding` transitions). Next free slot in the batch takes it.

## Fix round on PR #7291 — `Type Check` was red, now green

**What was red.** `@object-ui/console#type-check` (run 33588494358 / job 100117481182), three errors from one cause:

```
../../vitest.config.mts(311,7): error TS2769: No overload matches this call.
../../vitest.config.mts(325,7): error TS2769: No overload matches this call.
vitest.config.ts(11,15): error TS2345: Argument of type 'UserConfig & …' is not assignable to parameter of type 'never'.
```

**Cause.** Inside the conditional spread that declares the new `dist` project, the literal `extends: true` widens to `boolean`, while `TestProjectConfiguration.extends` is `string | true | undefined`. The element then matched no `defineConfig` overload and the whole `projects` array degraded to `never[]`, which also took down the console entry two lines later.

**Fix.** `extends: true as const` — one token, plus a comment recording why the annotation is load-bearing so it does not get tidied away later. The three pre-existing projects were never affected: their `extends: true` sits in the plain array, where it never widened.

**Why my own gate set missed it.** The root `vitest.config.mts` is compiled by no type program of its own; `apps/console/vitest.config.ts` merges it, so the console's `tsc --noEmit` is the program that reads it. I ran the components, scripts and vitest-setup type programs before the first push, but not the console's. That is the real gap, and it is why the full `pnpm type-check` is now in the re-run set below rather than the narrowed one.

**Reproduced before fixing.** On an unbuilt worktree the real errors are unreachable behind 378 `TS2882`s, so the dependency closure was built through turbo first — the path CI takes. Before: exit 1, 3 `error TS` lines. After: exit 0, 0.

**Re-run at the fix commit `857c8afc5`**, exit codes captured by redirect-then-`$?`: console type-check exit 0 · components type-check exit 0 · `type-check:scripts` exit 0 · `type-check:vitest-setup` exit 0 · **full `pnpm type-check` (turbo, every package) exit 0 — `Tasks: 81 successful, 81 total`** · `pnpm test:dist` exit 0 (`Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tasks: 9 successful, 9 total`) · the lane still collects exactly 1 pin with `unit`/`dom`/`dom-heavy` at 0 · the opt-in refusal still fires (exit 1). No narrowing to declare — the full farm ran.

Pushed as a fix commit on the same branch (no rebase, no force-push); PR body has a "Fix round" section with the same evidence. PR stays draft.
